headline: Long Howie survives by 0.71, Jack Attack tops the ledger
lede: Week 4 came in loud and went out on a whisper, pardner. Long Howie and Super Troopers rode out of town still unbeaten, the Warthogs handed down the widest licking of the week at 32.71, and over at the other end of the street a ballgame got settled by 0.71. There's 9 weeks left in the regular season, so saddle up.
paragraphs: The Warthogs put 115.64 on the board and left Scott's Hype holding 82.93, a 32.71 gap that was the widest ditch dug all week. Javonte Williams hauled in 27.95 for the winners, which was plenty of cover for Courtland Sutton turning in 0.6, and Keon Coleman sat on the bench with 15.2 while a better lineup was worth 32.35 more. Scott's Hype got its best work from the Vikings defense at 16.0, and when your defense is your top hand, the trail's gone rocky. Warthogs ride at 3-1 on 3 straight; Scott's Hype settles at 2-2.

Jack Attack struck the richest vein in the territory, 142.41, enough to hold off Jrod's 122.38 by 20.03. Josh Allen led the winners with 22.46 and they still had Brian Robinson sitting on 24.55 in the wagon bed. Jrod did fine work up front, Bijan Robinson for 28.55 and Ernest Jones IV for a league-best 16.0 at linebacker, but Kyle Monangai watched the whole thing from the bench with 30.9, and a better lineup would have added 40.2, the sorriest sortin' job of the week. Jack Attack evens up at 2-2, Jrod slides to 1-3 on a 3-game slide.

e-mans revenge scratched out 99.24 to take sisu's 83.53 by 15.71, and it came with a story: Matthew Stafford went for 17.44 while Aaron Rodgers sat benched with 22.18, a better lineup being worth 15.39 more. Ja'Marr Chase managed 2.55 for the winners and they won anyway, which tells you all you need about sisu's afternoon. sisu got 16.78 from Bo Nix and a flat 0.0 from Kenyon Sadiq at tight end. e-mans revenge gets its first mark at 1-3; sisu falls back to 2-2.

HAWKSRULE scraped by with 88.65 against Norskes U Betcha's 74.04, the lowest total in the territory this week, by 14.61. Dak Prescott carried the freight with 26.65 and that about did it. Norskes U Betcha started Saquon Barkley for 1.3 and kept Tyler Shough and his 19.77 parked in the shade, where a better lineup was worth 18.23. Both outfits sit at 1-3, and the Norskes have lost 3 in a row.

Super Troopers stayed perfect, 139.01 to 126.15 over Aeil, a 12.86 margin in a shootout that would have won most weeks. Tetairoa McMillan was the big nugget at 32.2 for the winners, who got a flat 0.0 out of Azeez Al-Shaair and never flinched. Aeil had Kirk Cousins humming at 28.5 and the Packers defense idling on the bench with 18.0, though a better lineup was only worth 6.95 more. Super Troopers ride at 4-0; Aeil comes back to 2-2.

Justin's Bad Team put up 108.1 and took densmen's 99.59 by 8.51, which is a small gap to lose by when you leave this much in the wagon. Kenneth Walker III went for 30.75 for the winners, enough to carry a 0.0 from Case Keenum in the starting lineup. densmen got 27.34 from C.J. Stroud but benched the Giants defense and its 22.0, and a better lineup there was worth 27.05, more than 3 times the margin. Justin's Bad Team is 3-1 and winning 3 straight; densmen is 1-3.

WeBleedOrangeAndBlue edged Zihuatanejo 135.61 to 131.01, and the 4.6 between them was the second tightest in the territory. Joe Burrow went off for 38.06, the biggest single haul of the whole week, and even with Bryce Young and his 29.53 on the bench a better lineup was worth only 2.5, which is a lineup set near perfect. Zihuatanejo had CeeDee Lamb at 27.15 but left 32.23 worth of better arrangement on the table, Lamar Jackson and his 19.84 included. Both wagons roll on at 2-2.

Long Howie 113.99, Dart Star Orchestra 113.28. That's 0.71, the closest race in the territory, and it kept Long Howie unbeaten at 4-0. Jared Goff put up 31.04 for the winners; Dart Star Orchestra answered with Kyren Williams at 28.55 but started Rashee Rice for 0.0 and left the Buccaneers defense and its 11.0 on the bench, with a better lineup worth 2.45, which is to say the whole ballgame. Dart Star Orchestra drops to 1-3 and has lost 3 straight by the thinnest of hairs.
sign_off: 8 wagons make the playoff trail and there's 9 weeks of dust between here and there. Set your lineups, folks: the bench ain't where silver gets dug.
purse: The commissioner's purse pays 4 this week: Jack Attack takes $40 on 142.41, Super Troopers takes $20 on 139.01, WeBleedOrangeAndBlue takes $10 on 135.61, and Zihuatanejo collects $5 on 131.01. Tip your hat to all 4, that's honest money off an honest claim.
